notes.key_messages: In order that candidates receive credit where possible for incorrect answers, they should remember to show full working and reasoning. Incorrect answers without working cannot be given any credit, whereas partial credit can be awarded if a correct method is shown. Where candidates are asked to ‘show’ or ‘prove’ a result, marks will be lost if any essential steps in the argument are omitted. notes.general_comments: General comments The paper allowed the majority of candidates to show what they had learned and understood. Candidates did not however gather as many marks as expected on the early shorter questions. These were intended to be reasonably ‘routine’ and candidates in the future could benefit by ensuring that they are confident on ‘routine’ work. Conversely, many candidates were able to boost unimpressive performances on the first half of the paper by strong performances in the last two questions. The majority of scripts were well-presented but some candidates need to be reminded that they should work straight down the page rather than try to fit their answer to one question beside their answer to another
